item.title: Man City Make Significant Change to Pre-Match Preparations for Fulham Clash
item.description: Man City Make Significant Change to Pre-Match Preparations for Fulham Clash MATCH PREVIEW: Manchester City vs Fulham (Premier League) More Videos The Premier League giants will be looking to bounce back from a notably poor run in the English top-flight after the final international break of the calendar year as Fulham visit the Etihad Stadium. Prior to the latest pause for national team commitments, Manchester City followed up a record-breaking seven successive wins to start Enzo Maresca's era at the club with three defeats in a row. Aston Villa were the side to break that run with a 2-1 victory at Villa Park, before Brighton & Hove Albion took all three points from the Etihad in a 0-1 win, and Nottingham Forest scored their first home goals of the season with a 3-1 triumph at the City Ground. Those results leave Manchester City in third behind the aforementioned Seagulls and Premier League champions Arsenal , who hold a six-point advantage over the Sky Blues coming into the next portion of domestic fixtures. And as Enzo Maresca and Manchester City look to end a run of poor results on the pitch, changes have seemingly been made to the way the club prepare for matchday action at the Etihad Stadium. That is according to TNT Sports' broadcast of Manchester City against Fulham on Saturday lunchtime, with Enzo Maresca and his squad staying overnight at The Medlock Hotel within the Etihad Campus and connected to the Etihad Stadium itself ahead of matchday.

item.title: Stephen A. Smith admits ‘special’ player has changed his MVP vote recently
item.description: Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images The talk around who is leading the way for the MVP award is already heating up, with a number of players proving themselves to be playing at the absolute elite level. There are several players who fall into the conversation, but the two main names, for many people, are Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow. Josh Allen is certainly still in the conversation, but Stephen A. Smith has narrowed it down to the quarterbacks for the San Francisco 49ers and the Cincinnati Bengals. Smith had previously claimed his vote would go to Purdy following his excellent start to the season. However, the ESPN analyst has now admitted he has changed his mind over recent weeks and would give Burrow the advantage. Stephen A. Smith changes his MVP decision to Joe Burrow If the voting was now, it would be incredibly difficult to separate these two quarterbacks, with both of them showing their quality through the first half of the season. The advantages could be earned through their upcoming matchups against their expected postseason rivals. “Three weeks ago, it would have been Brock Purdy. I think Brock Purdy has been big-time this year. What I’m seeing from Joe Burrow right now, though, is special,” Smith said on First Take. “When I watch Joe Burrow throw this football, the man is just special. When he’s lined up behind centre, he’s a true difference-maker. You can see why Cincinnati went to back-to-back AFC Championship games and reached a Super Bowl with him as quarterback. Again, I’ve been Brock Purdy, Brock Purdy, Brock Purdy all season long because of the way he’s been playing, and I know he hasn’t had Mike Evans, which is another reason why I would give him the edge.” Burrow has led the Bengals to a five-game winning streak, with some favourable games ahead of them before the end of the season. A meeting with Patrick Mahomes in December is one many will have marked on their calendars, though. “When you look at Joe Burrow, though: A fifth consecutive game with at least four total touchdowns (the only other quarterback in NFL history to accomplish that was Peyton Manning in 2004). Seven consecutive games completing better than 70% of his passes,” Smith added. “It’s a phenomenal thing to watch right now, and the Cincinnati Bengals are winning football games. Taking all of that into consideration, Josh Allen and Brock Purdy obviously come to mind, but right now, I’ve got to give Joe Burrow the edge.” Read more: Jimmy Pitaro told what he must do right away to end the Troy Aikman and Joe Buck drama Dianna Russini shares seven words her NFL connections are telling her about Daniel Jones’ release by Indianapolis Colts ‘He’s done’ – Stephen A. Smith says there is no way back for Dallas Cowboys man who he simply cannot defend

item.title: Lehmann again denies knowing about sandpaper plot
item.description: Darren Lehmann is currently head coach of Northamptonshire [Getty Images] Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann has again vehemently denied any knowledge of the sandpaper plot, despite detailed allegations from Cameron Bancroft. In an ongoing row about the cheating scandal that took place in Australia's third Test against South Africa in 2018, Bancroft published a testimony running to more than 4,000 words in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday. At the same time, Lehmann was commentating on Australia's third one-day international against England, with Bancroft's account prompting him to leave the match early. On Saturday, Lehmann returned to broadcast for the BBC and Australian network ABC on the first T20 international in Melbourne. In an extended and emotional interview, addressing a range of Bancroft's claims, Lehmann said: He "didn't know" sandpaper was used by his Australia team. No coaches encouraged players to tamper with the ball before or during Australia's tour of South Africa in 2018. He is "not sure" about a walkie-talkie conversation with 12th man Peter Handscomb, which Bancroft claimed was an instruction from Lehmann to remove the sandpaper from the field. He resigned as Australia coach before he was sacked and did not sign a non-disclosure agreement. The fallout from the sandpaper scandal took him to a "really dark place". Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA Cummins' Australia captaincy at a crossroads - Agnew Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins Lehmann's renewed denial came on the same day Cricket Australia confirmed its "unanimous support" for Pat Cummins as Australia captain. Earlier, Cummins' fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood said he would consider his international future if the captain was forced to stand down. The debate about the sandpaper plot of 2018 was reopened two weeks ago by allegations in the autobiography of Usman Khawaja, who was part of the Australia team in Cape Town eight years ago. Khawaja's assertions that the whole team knew and should have taken responsibility have been supported by David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland, who were all on the tour. Warner, former captain Steve Smith and Bancroft were the only players punished for the cheating plot. It was Bancroft's testimony that heaped pressure on Lehmann, Cummins and the other members of the Australia team who played at Newlands. Cummins, Hazlewood and the rest of the Australia bowlers who played in Cape Town have always denied knowledge or involvement in the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Lehmann resigned as coach in the immediate aftermath of the South Africa tour, but the former Australia batter has always maintained his innocence. "Sandpaper, I didn't know," he said on Saturday. "Obviously, it was used. "The biggest thing with ball-tampering is it was just a bad time. Everyone, we all made mistakes. "But you've just got to try and move on. I know it's hard for everyone. item.title: Reacts Results: Win and you’re in their hearts
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Jacoby Brissett #11 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up prior to the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images All it took is one skin-of-their-teeth win over the New Orleans Saints to end a three-game losing skid, seize first place in the NFC South, and restore some faith from fans for the 4-5 Carolina Panthers. It helps, of course, that they are facing, at home, a 4-6 Baltimore Ravens team who is on their own five-game losing streak and is 1-5 in their last six games since Lamar Jackson was injured the first time for the season. This week they are giving newly acquired Jacoby Brissett his second start at quarterback for the Ravens and we’re all going to see what happens after that. Confidence rising 26% after a win in which the team arguably played a less complete game than they did in their loss to the Denver Broncos the week before has me wondering if this survey is just a lagging indicator of wins. They are the division leader with the worst record, with the NFC East leading New York Giants coming in as a close second at 5-3-1. Third place is a four way tie of 7-2 teams, including the Detroit Lions who currently sit atop a three-way 7-2 tie in the NFC North. There is no wonder we are seeing a lot of contemplation about changes to the playoff format when the Panthers are on track for a home playoff game (or whoever ‘wins’ the NFC South) and the NFC North is likely to have one or more teams with winning records miss the playoffs entirely. As for this week, most fans are unsurprisingly expecting a win. The Ravens have suffered injuries both natural and self-inflicted—looking at you, Marlon Humphrey—and are struggling to find a quarterback solution to keep their own playoff hopes on life support. The path to a wildcard berth is more open in the AFC, but extremely unlikely all the same. Have the Ravens given up as a team? Are they simply hopeless without Jackson? Are the Carolina Panthers capable of resurrecting any team’s lost pride and dignity with a surprisingly competitive game? A disciplined Panthers squad that is getting healthier are catching the ailing Ravens at the perfect time. Whether or not that is what we see on Sunday is anybody’s guess. item.title: Why Skip Bayless ‘can’t believe’ his own prediction for 49ers vs Vikings
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Skip Bayless has admitted he ‘can’t believe’ that he is backing the Minnesota Vikings to beat the San Francisco 49ers because that would mean Kirk Cousins wins a big game. The 49ers are 8-1 this season, with the Vikings not far behind them in the NFC with a 7-2 record. Minnesota have the best defence in the league this year and while they were previously struggling on the offence, they have now added Cousins as their new starting quarterback. The 38-year-old was in good form for the Las Vegas Raiders prior to his trade but Bayless does not seem to rate him when it comes to showing up in big games. In turn, he admitted on First Take that he ‘can’t believe’ he has picked the Vikings to win on Sunday. Bayless said: “The Minnesota Vikings will win this game. And I can’t believe I just said that because that means that Kirk Cousins will win a big game.” 2026 Minnesota Vikings are perfect for Kirk Cousins Cousins has struggled to perform in the postseason throughout his career. He has a 1-4 record and is 1-3 as the starting quarterback. However, Bayless also thinks that this Minnesota team is actually perfect for the ex-Raiders star due to their impressive defence. He continued: “I have spent 15 years saying Kirk Cousins is way overrated and way, way, way overpaid. Wait, he’s made more money than Tom Brady. “He’s 1 and 4 in the postseason. Dak was 4-0 against him when he was in Washington. But now, at age 38, Kirk Cousins has almost magically fallen into the perfect spot for him with the NFL’s best defence and the ability to reach back, recreate, turn back the clock to 2022 when those Vikings with Kirk Cousins at quarterback went 13-4 and Justin Jefferson was the offensive player of the year.” They have given up just 126 points this season, which is the best record in the league by some distance. Minnesota Vikings: 126 Jacksonville Jaguars: 144 Kansas City Chiefs: 156 Seattle Seahawks: 175 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 178 Their only real issue this season has been the offence. But while he has only played one game so far, Cousins seems to have had an immediate impact. He helped the Vikings score 30 points against the Green Bay Packers last week, which was the first time they scored 30-plus in a game since the opening week of 2026/27. item.title: Juventus must focus on May, not August
item.description: TURIN, ITALY - NOVEMBER 18: Juventus head coach Luciano Spalletti during a Juventus FC training session at JTC on November 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images) | Juventus FC via Getty Images Here’s a question right off the bat: Coming out of the international break and looking at the rest of the 2026-27 season ahead, what is the best way Juve can make the most of their remaining fixtures? Too often Juventus have approached transfer windows as opportunities to solve every problem, everywhere, all at once. Though, I accept, what we have seen as the problem has not always been what they have seen as the problem, and let’s not even start on what the “solutions” have looked like on some occasions. Perhaps I am best left, at this early stage, to posit that our transfer mentality has not always lead us to greener pastures. This January needs to be different. Looking to start our run for the rest of the year now, we need to be strategic and ruthless when it comes to the next couple of months. Bluntly, our objective is not to build the Juventus of 2029 in the next six weeks. That ship has sailed — and I think we can all agree that it has floundered somewhat mid-journey. It is not even to build the Juventus of next season. I think the best, the clearest, the most ruthless thing we can do now is to maximize the Juventus that takes the field between February and May. Every decision, whether tactical, sporting, or financial, should be judged against a simple question: Will this help Juventus win more points during over the next six weeks and then into the second half of this season? If the answer is no, it can wait. Before we even think about making signings, we need to understand exactly what we already have, and what we are going to do with it. Several key questions must be answered before Christmas. The first concerns Kenan Yıldız. This young man has shown flashes of brilliance, he stands ready to become the face of the club. But — how many times have we read that word in conjunction with Juve — there is a significant difference between a prospect and a star. If Yıldız is ready to become the centerpiece of the attack, recruitment should focus on supporting him. If he is not yet at that stage, Juventus may need additional firepower. The second sits with Khéphren Thuram. Perhaps no player embodies the future more than this midfielder. If Thuram establishes himself as one of Serie A’s elite midfielders, the club gains a foundational piece around which a title-winning side can be built. If not, resources may need to be allocated differently. The management team should spend the weeks before January evaluating the squad with complete honesty. Championship challenges are built on clarity, not hope. Which brings us to goals — or the lack of them. When the transfer window opens, Juventus should focus on one issue above all others: increasing their goal output. Defensively, the team looks relatively solid. N

item.title: How McLaren tried to mitigate its Las Vegas F1 top speed deficit
item.description: Motorsport photo Despite what was a respectable result on a circuit that accentuated the MCL40's flaws without rewarding its virtues, Lando Norris was not best pleased with how Friday at the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend. “We're just shocking on the straights,” said Norris shortly after qualifying fifth, just under eight tenths behind polesitter Kimi Antonelli, who is set to drop five places for an engine penalty, elevating Norris to fourth on the grid. The long straights and low downforce demands meant the Las Vegas Strip circuit was never going to be the strongest track for this car, as foreshadowed by McLaren's muted form on the circuit's nearest comparisons in Monza and Baku. But McLaren's deficit in Vegas was still surprisingly vast, at least to Antonelli, with Norris and Oscar Piastri routinely 20km/h down on the circuit's long Las Vegas Boulevard as well as the final straight towards the finish. Differences so massive are rarely just down to one single factor, and that also proved to be the case on Friday. Despite regular upgrades, the MCL40 remains relatively draggy and aerodynamically inefficient, which is compounded by the team's pre-season choice to go for a shorter gearing, costing it top-end grunt on circuits with extremely long straights. Like all teams, McLaren had the option to make one mid-season change to its gear ratios, but decided against it because its shorter gearing would still stand it in good stead on other circuits. In Vegas, though, the team had to pay the price. "Definitely we had some concern in terms of how suitable the demands of this circuit would be for our car," team principal Andrea Stella replied when asked by Motorsport.com whether the squad's deficit was more severe than anticipated. "This is not only the top speed, it is also the top speed that is combined with the towing that everyone is trying to do. So, you go in operating regimes of the engine that with our ratios is not ideal. We know that the drag from an aerodynamic point of view is not a point of strength. We have seen traits that are similar to Monza, to Baku. And in all conditions we were not particularly competitive." Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren With slipstreaming so crucial, as evidenced by the positional tactics that dominated Q3 and cost the likes of Isack Hadjar and George Russell , McLaren tried to compensate for its lack of top speed by more aggressively chasing the tow. "What we have done better here is to mitigate this by having really good positioning," Stella added. "The car was pretty much where we wanted it to be in qualifying. And this definitely helped. Because I have to say that it seems like with these regulations the drag reduction when you follow one car or even multiple cars is more than in the past. And therefore, there is an even higher incentive to be positioned in the right place." item.title: JuJu Watkins issues WNBA draft update after dropping 36 points for USC
item.description: Photo by Melina Pizano/Getty Images Fresh off dropping 36 points for USC, JuJu Watkins finally addressed where she stands on the WNBA draft. JuJu Watkins didn’t take long to remind everyone why she’s the consensus No. 1 pick for the 2027 WNBA Draft. With the Toronto Tempo winning the draft lottery after their rough 11–33 debut season, mock drafts already have the expansion team locking in the USC star, assuming she actually declares. Coming off an ACL tear, Watkins erased any doubts in No. 4 USC’s 78–69 win over Baylor, taking over the game with 36 points, 11 rebounds, six steals, and four assists in 39 minutes. JuJu Watkins is still undecided on the WNBA Following the win, reporters inevitably asked JuJu Watkins about her plans for the 2027 WNBA Draft, and she made it clear she’s keeping her focus strictly on USC for now: She said: “I really can’t say what I’m doing because I don’t know. I’m just locked in on everything we have going on here, honestly.” Through five games this season, JuJu Watkins is putting up video-game numbers, averaging 26.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.8 steals, 3.6 assists, and 1.2 blocks a night on 46.5% shooting. She’s topped 20 points every single time out, highlighted by a 32-point, 16-rebound clinic against Utah State and her season-high 36 points with 11 boards to take down Baylor. item.title: ESPN Analyst Urges 'Imperfect Prospect' Arch Manning to Not Declare for NFL 2027 Draft in Blunt Message
item.description: NCAA, College League, USA Football: Texas at Texas A&M Nov 30, 2024 College Station, Texas, USA Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning warms up prior to the game against the Texas A&M Aggies. The Longhorns defeated the Aggies 17-7 at Kyle Field. College Station Kyle Field Texas USA, EDITORIAL USE ONLY PUBLICATIONxINxGERxSUIxAUTxONLY Copyright: xMariaxLysakerx 20241230_mcl_la6_058 ©IMAGO/Imagn Images It’s safe to say that Arch Manning has been under immense pressure to deliver performances because of his last name, hailing from the same family as Peyton and Eli Manning. Amid his lack of performance, an ESPN analyst thinks he might need to change teams for better results, and has deterred him from declaring for the 2027 NFL Draft. “I think Arch Manning is an imperfect prospect like a lot of these kids are,” analyst Booger McFarland said on the Dan Patrick Show Friday. “And I think his ability to play quarterback position sometimes is really good and other times, it’s really bad.” McFarland then touched upon an added variable, which is the “juxtaposition” of what was expected from another Manning in football versus what the world is getting right now, leading to the criticism the 22-year-old is facing. However, the Texas QB’s talent cannot be undermined. “I think that Arch is a super talent. He’s 6’3, 225. He’s athletic. He can throw it. He’s got the lineage. He’s got all the things, but he doesn’t quite put it all together,” added McFarland. Should Arch Manning wait another year before chasing NFL stardom? Get insider analysis on why top experts believe patience could be his biggest advantage. Subscribe for the latest quarterback development stories. Manning has been under heavy scrutiny, as fans and analysts have seen inaccuracies in his form. In 10 games this season, Manning has completed 187 of 289 pass attempts for 2,189 yards and thrown 19 touchdowns. He has also thrown 10 interceptions in the process. If we look at his career with the Texas Longhorns, he has yet to win a national championship with the team. His career has ranged from being a potential Heisman Trophy winner to succumbing to harsh criticism. Now, McFarland thinks Manning can do way better with a different program and a different voice in his head during plays. “He’s been at Texas for four years, and he’s heard the same voice over and over in Steve Sarkisian. I think if you’re Cooper and you’re Eli and you’re Archie, and you’re Payton, and you’re the Manning family, I think you tell Arch, ‘Hey, let’s go hear from a different voice.’ Maybe it’s in Ole Miss (Rebels). Maybe it’s Kentucky (Wildcats) with Will Stein,” McFarland continued. McFarland’s assessment implies that Manning would take up his fifth year of college eligibility next year. There has been plenty of speculation about whether Manning would play another year of college football, as he does have an extra year of eligibility, or if he’ll decide that it’s time for the big transition. item.title: NCAA Tournament second round preview: No. 2-seed Maryland men’s soccer vs. NC State
item.description: After finishing the regular season with a 12-5-1 record and making it to the Big Ten tournament semifinals, No. 2-seed Maryland men’s soccer enters its 32nd NCAA tournament under head coach Sasho Cirovski. As the tournament begins, Cirovski is looking for the Terps to play their best soccer going forward. “I think it comes down to playing your best at the right time,” Cirovski said. “All year I’ve looked at some of our difficult moments as an opportunity to get stronger and tougher and I certainly hope that what we see at this point in the year.” The Terps hold home-field advantage for their second-round matchup against NC State. The game will be played at 1 p.m. Sunday at Ludwig Field and will be televised on ESPN Plus. “I think you’re seeing two elite teams,” Cirovski said. “I think it’s a very big matchup in the round of 32.” NC State (8-6-6, 1-3-4 ACC) In 2025, the Wolfpack had an outstanding season, finishing with a 16-3-4 record and making it all the way to the national championship. They ultimately fell to a Washington team that had knocked out Maryland earlier in the tournament. Donavan Phillip, who won the MAC Hermann Trophy after leading the nation with 19 goals, along with defender Nikola Markovic and goalkeeper Logan Erb departed in the offseason. Despite the roster turnover, NC State earned its third NCAA tournament appearance in as many years under head coach Marc Hubbard. This season, the Wolfpack faced more turbulence after finishing the regular season with a single conference win and the 11-seed in the ACC tournament. However, NC State defeated six-seed Virginia Tech and three-seed Wake Forest to make it to the semifinal before falling to the eventual champions, North Carolina. In the first round of the NCAA tournament, the Wolfpack defeated College of Charleston, 2-1, on Thursday after two second-half goals from Hayato Takayama and Tyler Caton. Entering Sunday’s match, NC State is unbeaten in eight of its last nine games, including a 3-1-3 record against six NCAA tournament teams during that stretch. Players to watch Aidan Payne, fifth-year forward, No. 15 — Payne has taken a significant step forward as the Wolfpack’s leading attacker, posting a team-high 10 goals and 21 points with 43 shots — 20 of them being on goal. Payne has earned career highs in each of those categories this year and his 10 goals are fourth-most in the ACC. item.title: Virgil van Dijk has ‘no idea’ whether he will extend contract at Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk remains uncertain of whether he will remain at the club beyond the end of the season. The 35-year-old centre-back is approaching the final six months of his contract , which expires next summer. He believes that he can keep playing at the top level for “many more years” but says he has “no idea” whether that will be at Anfield as Liverpool’s decision-makers continue to ponder over a fresh offer. "The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk told Sky Sports. "Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see. At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either. "But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then. "But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years. "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer." Virgil van Dijk’s future is up in the air with his contract expiring in the summer (Getty) Van Dijk has won two Premier League titles, including the club’s first in 30 years, as well as a Champions League with Liverpool, stamping his mark as one of the greatest centre-backs in the English top flight’s history since his £75m arrival from Southampton in 2018. He is one of the last remaining figures from Jurgen Klopp ’s side that won every trophy there was to win between 2019 and 2022, with Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson notably bidding emotional farewells at the end of last season. Asked about the prospect of having to say goodbye to Anfield himself, Van Dijk said: " Well, yeah, probably for me the most and the family because it's been an incredible time. "But I don't look too far in the future and that's been, in my opinion, also a little bit of a success. I won't change it now either. "Whatever happens, happens. Let's see." Liverpool host Manchester United for new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first game on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez renews Negreira case pressure as Barcelona face fresh scrutiny: ‘This is a widespread fraud’
item.description: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez renews Negreira case pressure as Barcelona face fresh scrutiny: ‘This is a widespread fraud’ Barcelona have once again found themselves at the centre of the Negreira controversy after Florentino Perez used Real Madrid’s Annual General Meeting to question the club’s historical payments to former refereeing official Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira and demand further accountability. However, several of the Real Madrid president’s accusations need to be considered carefully alongside Barcelona’s continued explanation of the payments and their official response to UEFA’s communication. Perez made the Negreira case the central subject of his address to Real Madrid members on Saturday, November 21, arguing that the controversy affects the integrity of Spanish football. He also questioned the involvement of La Liga and the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), claiming that Real Madrid had taken greater responsibility for pursuing the investigation. In case you are unaware, the controversy concerns payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to Negreira, who was vice-president of the Technical Committee of Referees (CTA). Barcelona have acknowledged the payments but maintained that they were for technical reports and advisory services relating to referees and not to influence match officials. Florentino Perez demands further investigation in Negreira controversy Perez began his comments by insisting that the consequences of the Negreira case extend beyond Real Madrid. “The Negreira case is not a problem for Real Madrid . We may well be its main victim, but this is a widespread fraud that affected all national and international competitions, which are interconnected. Florentino Perez has launched a fresh attack on Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “It is a problem for everyone involved in the competition and for the institutions that oversee it,” he pressed. The Real Madrid president subsequently added that he wanted the investigation to continue until those responsible had been held accountable. “I will not stop until all those responsible have been held to account,” he added. Perez then questioned why other football institutions had not shown the same determination to investigate the matter. “It is difficult to understand why, given that this is a problem for everyone, Madrid is the only party keen to see this case investigated to the full. “This directly calls into question the rest of those involved, particularly La Liga and the RFEF. “Their primary responsibility is to safeguard the integrity of the competition. “They have done nothing with regard to UEFA, and it has had to be Real Madrid that gathered the information and lodged the complaint with UEFA,” he added. He subsequently directed further criticism at the two organisations, adding, “The Federation is at the very heart of this case, whilst LaLiga remains completely inactive. item.title: Harry Kane Injury Bayern Munich: Star Out for Several Months
item.description: TOPSHOT - Bayern Munich's English forward #09 Harry Kane holds his leg after getting a knock during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and FC Cologne on November 20, 2026. (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP via Getty Images) Getty Bayern Munich have been dealt a major blow, and England could be next to feel the consequences. Bayern Munich confirmed on Friday that star striker Harry Kane has a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle, with the club announcing that its star striker will miss the next few months. The diagnosis comes after Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into Bayern’s 1-1 draw with Cologne, leaving the Bundesliga leaders without their most important attacking player for a significant stretch of the season. The 33-year-old England captain had only recently celebrated winning the Ballon d’Or and becoming his country’s most-capped men’s player. Now, instead of building on those achievements, he faces a lengthy spell of rehabilitation. Harry Kane Injury Bayern Munich Confirms Is a Syndesmosis Tear Bayern confirmed the diagnosis after an examination by the club’s medical department. The statement described a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in Kane’s left ankle and said the forward would be sidelined for “the next few months.” That wording does not establish an exact return date. However, reporting from Sky Germany puts the expected absence at approximately three months, which would take Kane into the latter part of the season. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl has also indicated that the club is still assessing whether surgery will be necessary. Kane was replaced by Tom Bischof in the 20th minute of Friday’s match at the Allianz Arena. Bayern eventually drew 1-1 , with Mikey Moore scoring for Cologne and Nathaniel Brown equalizing before halftime. The result left Bayern on 22 points from 10 Bundesliga matches, just one point ahead of Borussia Dortmund. How Much Will Bayern Munich Miss Harry Kane? The timing could hardly be worse for Vincent Kompany’s team. Bayern have four Champions League league-phase matches remaining, beginning with the trip to Lille on November 25. They then host Slavia Prague on December 8 before visiting Manchester United on January 20 and welcoming Real Betis on January 27. Bayern also have a DFB-Pokal round-of-16 meeting with Hertha Berlin scheduled for December 1. In the Bundesliga, the club faces a demanding run of fixtures through the winter, including matches against Bayer Leverkusen and Borussia Dortmund. An absence lasting around three months could cost Bayern a substantial portion of their domestic campaign. The injury also adds to Bayern’s existing problems. Manuel Neuer, Alphonso Davies, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz and Ismael Saibari have all been among the players unavailable, while Michael Olise was also forced off against Cologne with a forefoot injury. item.title: Kenny Atkinson’s Bold James Harden Claim Sparks Debate After Cavs Star Surpasses Kobe Bryant With 50-Point Masterclass
item.description: ©Credit - Getty Last night, James Harden reminded the NBA world of what he’s capable of. Fans roared with applause, but spared him little respect. The Beard delivered one of his finest performances in a Cleveland Cavaliers uniform at 37. While his historic scoring display deservedly attracted attention, head coach Kenny Atkinson’s post-game assessment became another talking point. His bold claim about Harden’s place among basketball’s greatest players did not convince everyone, with fans quickly resorting to trolling. James Harden exploded for 51 points as the Cavs defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in their NBA Cup matchup. More importantly, it was Harden’s 26th career 50-point game, moving him past his childhood idol, Kobe Bryant (25), for the third-most in NBA history. Only Wilt Chamberlain (118) and Michael Jordan (31) remain ahead of him. James Harden just etched his name alongside basketball royalty, and Kenny Atkinson's take on what it means is dividing the league. Stay locked in for the analysis that matters. Coach Atkinson was understandably impressed. “Guy’s special. We gotta, I know, you know, everyone wants a perfect, but we gotta appreciate this guy,” Atkinson said at the post-game presser . The Cavaliers coach went beyond praising Harden’s performance and made a rather ambitious assessment of his career. “ You know, like, this guy is top 10 of all time . I know I appreciate every day coaching him. It’s an honor. I really mean that. Doesn’t happen to a lot of coaches to get to coach a guy like that.” However, the statement quickly attracted skepticism on social media, with fans offering different reasons why they disagreed with the coach’s assessment. James Harden’s top-10 claim draws trolls One fan questioned Atkinson’s credibility, writing, “Top 10?!?!? 😂😂 this is coming from the same guy that said they analytically beat the Knicks in the playoffs btw.” The reference goes back to Cleveland’s 2025-26 Eastern Conference Finals defeat against the New York Knicks. With the Cavaliers trailing 3-0, Atkinson argued that his team had won two of the three games based on expected-score analytics. Although he was referring to shot quality and statistical projections rather than actual results, the comment became a widely mocked soundbite . To make matters worse, the Cavs suffered a sweep. Another fan questioned Harden’s overall contribution this season, commenting, “Top 10 in what exactly?? No real accomplishment. Cleveland has been terrible this season, he has been pretty mid before tonight…” There is some context behind that frustration. Cleveland entered Friday with a 8-8 record. Meanwhile, Harden was averaging 16.2 points on just 38.5% shooting through his first 15 appearances. His 51-point explosion was exceptional. But one performance does not erase an inconsistent start to the campaign. item.title: “Gonna Happen Ruthlessly”: FOX Analyst Predicts Reported New AD Trev Alberts’ Plan to Fire Kyle Whittingham as He Prepares To Take Over at Michigan
item.description: Michigan © Instagram/umichfootball Rumors about Kyle Whittingham’s future at Michigan continue to swirl as the program struggles to string together wins. Michigan is 5-5, and many believe the veteran coach won’t get more than one season with the Wolverines. With only two games left, against undefeated UCLA and Ohio State, they could end up with a losing record this season. With the Wolverines reportedly hiring Trev Alberts as their new athletic director to replace Warde Manuel, a series of changes seems underway at Michigan. Analysts think Whittingham could be one of the biggest losers in the new status quo. On his podcast Friday, analyst Aaron Torres predicted that the coach would be fired if he doesn’t win his next two games. “fast-forward to this Michigan situation. I think it’s going to happen, I think it’s going to happen quickly, I think it’s going to happen ruthlessly,” said Torres. “why you wanted to get Trev Alberts hired and in the door is so that he can meet with the people that he has to meet with to get the money that he needs to get to get Kyle Whittingham out the door.” Torres said he doesn’t expect Whittingham to be fired before or immediately after the UCLA game, but predicted that if the Wolverines don’t change how they play, the coach is unlikely to remain at the helm. “If there isn’t like immediate turnaround, as in it happens really quick and there clearly is a better product on the field, I believe Kyle Whittingham is getting fired after this season.” Unnamed source on why Kyle Whittingham is struggling at Michigan Kyle Whittingham was brought to Ann Arbor to fix a program whose coach had recently been fired for cause. The move was universally praised as the right one for the school. Fast forward almost a year, and Whittingham is struggling mightily. The parent of a Michigan player said the coach’s inability to adapt to the Wolverines’ culture was the main reason for his struggles: “Michigan is a different breed,” the parent told the athletic. “ You’ve got to embrace their culture. You embrace Michigan. If you don’t, No. 1, the fans will rip you apart.” Regardless of the reason, Whittingham’s struggles are one of the most unexpected turns of the 2026 season. item.title: Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil
item.description: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage. Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people. “It’s something never seen before, a movie scene,” Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media. “Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished,” he said. The hospital’s roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred. The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3 am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said. Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located. Another 32 municipalities also reported damage. This handout picture released by Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defence Department shows the damage caused by strong winds in Tupancireta, Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, on November 20, 2026. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm. “We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing,” Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defense, told Radio Gaucha. Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114 kilometers per hour (70 miles per hour) during the storm. Civil defense described the storm as a “supercell,” which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the possibility that a tornado hit the city. State officials have allocated about $330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster. Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornadoes. AFP The post Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Andoni Iraola reveals Liverpool return plan for Conor Bradley & Giovanni Leoni as Hugo Ekitike timeline confirmed
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-CRYSTAL PALACE-LIVERPOOL - AFP Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has provided a comprehensive update on the fitness of several key first-team stars as they continue their respective paths to recovery. The Reds boss detailed the integration process for long-term absentees Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni while clarifying the situation regarding Hugo Ekitike. Bradley and Leoni closing in on comeback Liverpool have been handed a significant boost as defenders Bradley and Leoni have returned to outdoor training at the AXA Training Centre this week. Bradley has been out of action since January, while Leoni has faced an even longer road to recovery after being sidelined since last September, but both are now working alongside their teammates again. Iraola expressed his satisfaction with their progress as the medical staff look to integrate them back into the senior setup. "With Conor and Gio we are thinking about how we can get the next steps for them," explained the Spaniard on the club's official website . The focus now shifts toward building up their match fitness after such extensive periods on the treatment table. "And we think they will have two weeks on and off the group, let’s say. And then it is going to be a matter of whether we organise something behind closed doors, 11 v 11. Or they straight away play with the U21s, that is also a very good option. I think before they start playing with us they have to go through that, yes." Ekitike targeting New Year return While the defensive duo are nearing a competitive return, Ekitike still has some way to go before he is ready to feature for the first team again. The striker has been recovering from an Achilles rupture suffered during a match at Anfield back in April, which has kept the club's number 22 out of action for several months. The Liverpool boss reiterated that the original plan for Ekitike’s return remains firmly in place despite his recent work behind the scenes. "The plan has always been January and that hasn’t changed," Iraola confirmed. "If things go incredibly well, he can plan earlier, which would be much better for everyone. But right now we still focus on January and that is the plan." The striker's rehab slower than injured duo Iraola confirmed that Ekitike is slightly behind Bradley and Leoni in his rehabilitation schedule, but the club remains optimistic about his progress. The coaching staff is currently working toward a specific window for his comeback, ensuring the player is not rushed back too quickly following such a devastating physical setback during the previous campaign. There was even consideration given to the forward during the registration process for European competition earlier this term. “Hugo is behind [Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni], of course, and I think the target with Hugo has always been January. item.description: Good morning! Win a championship today. Coming up: ⚽️ A women’s soccer launchpad 😬 Indy drops Jones 🧠 Improve your attention span Titles: Ready for launch Ring the bells, text the group chat, hit pause on Grand Theft Auto VI: We’ve got a championship game today, folks! item.description: Los Angeles Lakers at Orlando Magic, Orlando, Florida, USA Orlando, Florida, USA, March 21, 2026, Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James 9 at the Kia Center. The Lakers front office is signaling a shift in strategy. Subscribe to stay ahead of LA's next moves and roster decisions. item.title: 'That is the most ridiculous question to ask' - Ruud Gullit refuses to choose between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo
item.description: GOLF-EPGA-NED - AFP Former Netherlands midfielder Ruud Gullit has refused to take sides in the long-running debate between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, dismissing the comparison as ridiculous. The 1987 Ballon d'Or winner instead insisted he was simply glad to watch both superstars compete before steering the conversation towards Argentine legend Diego Maradona. Dutch icon rejects rivalry question Gullit pushed back when asked whether Messi or Ronaldo ranks higher during an appearance on Sports Uncensored . Host Simon Jordan closed their interview by pressing the former AC Milan star to name the better player. When reminded that Ballon d'Or voting demands one winner, the Dutchman declined to pick either man and cited an old rival instead. Gullit gives blunt studio response Few retired players escape being asked about the pair, and Gullit reacted immediately when Jordan raised the topic on the show: "Come on. No, that is the most ridiculous question to ask. I have seen these two battling each other for such a long, long time." Preferring to enjoy their rivalry rather than rank them, he explained: "I am happy that I've seen it. Both of them." When Jordan noted Gullit had once been named the best himself, he replied: "On that moment on, if you would ask me who was the best player when I won it, I would have said Diego Maradona." The host laughed and conceded the point was reasonable, though not what he wanted. Maradona remains his ultimate benchmark Naming Maradona was no improvisation from Gullit, who faced the Napoli talisman several times with Milan. During a tribute at The Best gala in December 2020 shortly after Maradona's death, he recalled: "I remember the first time I faced him. [Roberto] Donadoni and [Carlo] Ancelotti were trying to take the ball off him and couldn't. He was incredibly strong and technically brilliant. He was also a leader, always talking to his teammates so they would give more." Noting how opponents targeted him physically, Gullit said: "They tried to take him out of the game with kicks, and they managed it once, when Goikoetxea injured him." He added: "They couldn't stop him. Imagine if he had today's protection, the video, the cameras and all that. I faced him and I can say he is the best in history." Greatest player debate rolls on Comparisons between Messi and Ronaldo show no sign of fading among supporters and former players as their careers wind down. For Gullit, however, the standard for football's greatest was set decades ago by the opponent he battled firsthand in Serie A. Until anyone surpasses that memory, the Dutchman is unlikely to change his verdict.

The Merengues were in fine form before the international window, stringing together an eight-game winning streak across all competitions, with victories over the likes of Barcelona, RB Leipzig, and AS Roma along the way. Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 in their final match before the break and will now be looking forward to carry on from where they left off against Celta Vigo. It will not be straightforward, though, considering that the Galicians have posed a tough challenge to the Spanish capital club in the recent past and even beat them at the Santiago Bernabeu last season. At the heart of the defence, Antonio Rudiger could be in line for a rare starting opportunity, partnering up with Dean Huijsen . Midfield Real Madrid were handed a major concern during the international break as two key midfielders, Bernardo Silva and Aurelien Tchouameni , returned from the national team due to physical setbacks. Much to the relief of Mourinho & co., the problems turned out to be nothing serious and the pair has been included in the squad list to face Celta tonight. In fact, given their importance to the team, it is likely that both Bernardo and Tchouameni feature from the get-go at the Santiago Bernabeu later today. Bernardo has become an important player for Mourinho. item.title: The RUNDOWN: Everything you need to know about the Bears in Week 11 against the Saints
item.description: (Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images) LAKE FOREST, Ill. — The Bears’ bye week is over. It’s back to football and a stretch run that includes four NFC North games. But first comes the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field. “It’s all about winning this week,” coach Ben Johnson said. “We’ll worry about everything else when it’s time. It’s not time for that. There’s still eight games to be played and this is the most important one because it’s the next one.” With that in mind, here is everything you need to know about the Bears from the podium to the locker room to the injury report in Week 11. 1. Quarterback Caleb Williams doesn’t feel like he’s playing through an injury right now. But he’s still got to manage his right hamstring going forward. “Once you have a severe injury like that and you come back and you didn’t have it before, you have to keep consistently doing rehab over and over again throughout the weeks to be able to just keep it strong and keep it up to date and make it stronger to get back to where it was, because it takes a while,” he said. “It’s not being overworked or anything like that but (it’s) just being able to focus on it throughout the weeks.” The bye week certainly helped, too. “It was good,” Williams said. “It’s always good to get that time off. Especially since the injury, I’ve been go, go, go, whether it’s rehab, whether it’s film, whether it’s the games (and) obviously, the short weeks, the long weeks, anything like that, schedules changing around. “It was good to get some time off and reset mentally and physically. I didn’t do ‘nothing’ but just had a little bit more time to be able to relax and maybe not move as much.” 2. The bye week also came at the perfect time for receiver Luther Burden III. Burden suffered a concussion against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 at Soldier Field. But he passed all protocols by the time the team returned to practice on Monday. Burden practiced in full every day. He doesn’t have an injury designation for Sunday. “Luther’s huge for this offense,” quarterback Caleb Williams said on Tuesday. “I mean, he took a 40-, 50-yard, 60-yard pass to the crib on a 5-yard route. So that’s who Luther is. I talk about him each week that we get up here or anything like that that I get the chance to just because he’s special for us. He’s explosive, he makes plays, he’s going to keep making plays, he’s going to keep getting up and celebrating, bringing the energy and the juice for us as a team, as an offense. “And so him being cleared is exciting. I was checking up on him a few times over the little break that we had and he said he’s felt good.” 3. The Bears are excited to have running back Kyle Monangai back on the field. It’s been a long time coming, too. Monangai last played in Week 4 against the New York Jets. He had a career-high 30 carries that day for 146 yards and two touchdowns. But then came his turf toe problems. “Hopefully that is a great boost for us,” offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. “We’ll see

item.title: Takeaways from Maryland men’s basketball’s 62-45 victory over Wagner
item.description: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 20: Head coach Buzz Williams of the Maryland Terrapins talks with Andre Mills #7 during the second half against the Wagner Seahawks at Xfinity Center on November 20, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was far from pretty, but Maryland men’s basketball earned another home nonconference win Friday, beating Wagner 62-45. Pharrel Payne led the way for the Terps, with his 25-point, 13-rebound double-double contributing more than a third of the team’s total for each statistic. Andre Mills was the only other player to reach double figures, and no other Terp had more than four rebounds. That result sends the Terps off to Las Vegas. While there, most readers that filled out the Testudo Times Reacts survey wager the Terps will win one or two games. Here are three takeaways from Friday’s tune-up game. High volume from the perimeter to no avail After producing its highest 3-point percentage in the last eight games during Monday’s win, Maryland tried to replicate that success early on. Seven of the Terps’ first nine shots came from deep. They made just one attempt. DJ Wagner swung the ball up top to a wide open Mills late in the shot clock of Maryland’s first possession, and the redshirt sophomore drilled the 3-pointer. While Mills has shown improvements over the last two games after an early-season slump, he was the Terps’ main contributor from deep Friday — Mills had three of the five makes. Maryland missed its next seven 3-pointers, with five different players recording a shot. Even Tomislav Buljan, who made just eight triples last season at New Mexico, attempted his first look from behind the arc this year three minutes into the game. The Terps’ nine-minute drought without a made 3-pointer was ended by an unlikely source: Baba Oladotun. After starting the season 0-of-4 from deep, the freshman drained both of his 3-point looks Friday. First-career three for Baba 👌 📺: Subscribe/watch on B1G+ https://t.co/dBmMXZMqhl pic.twitter.com/jXpPqG0HU4 — Maryland Men’s Basketball (@TerrapinHoops) November 21, 2026 But outside of Oladotun and Mills, no other Maryland player made a shot from behind the arc. Mike McNair Jr., who entered the game with a team-high nine 3-pointers on a 56.25% shooting clip, couldn’t connect on his four attempts from downtown. While the looks weren’t falling, the Terps kept hoisting 3-point shots. Maryland hit just one of its eight attempts in the second half, with Oladotun’s make coming 15 minutes after halftime. Despite the Terps’ 22.7% 3-point percentage Friday, nearly half of their shots came from distance — something that isn’t alarming for head coach Buzz Williams. “I don’t necessarily think that our volume of threes has been wrong. 35% of our shots have been from [deep],” Williams said after Monday’s game. item.title: Pat Murphy Updates Viral Jake Bauers Yankees Jab After Red Sox Contract
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 17: Jake Bauers #18 of the Boston Red Sox speaks during a press conference announcing his contract agreement on November 17, 2026 at Fenway Park in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox/Getty Images) Getty Images The Boston Red Sox made an early offseason investment in a player coming off the best season of his major league career, adding another significant piece to their plans for 2027. Jake Bauers, who helped the Milwaukee Brewers capture their first World Series championship, is headed to Boston after a remarkable career turnaround that nearly never happened. The move also brings an interesting subplot involving Brewers manager Pat Murphy, whose comments about Bauers and the New York Yankees became one of the more memorable viral moments of Milwaukee’s championship celebration. Murphy had previously made headlines for taking an unfiltered shot at the Yankees while discussing Bauers’ impending free agency, and the first baseman’s new contract gave the manager a chance to revisit his message to his former player. Now that Bauers has officially landed a lucrative deal with Boston, Murphy has offered a more thoughtful update to his parting message. “Is it hard losing Jake? Yeah, he was a huge part of that room for the last three years,” Murphy said following news of Bauers’ contract agreement with the Red Sox, per a clip shared by Fox Sports’ Hunter Baumgardt . “I’m excited for Jake, and we move on. It isn’t all about us, it is about some guys getting rewarded.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Red Sox Finally Close Ugly Mookie Betts Chapter WIth Unceremonious Cut Pat Murphy Revisits Boston Red Sox Slugger Message After New York Yankees Hot Mic Moment Goes Viral Murphy’s viral remarks came during Milwaukee’s World Series celebration, when Bauers handed him the baseball from the final out. The manager suggested that Bauers would soon become wealthy in free agency, suggesting he would soon sign with the New York Yankees. “You’re going to be a rich f---er,” Murphy told Bauers, according to ESPN . “Just remember when you were on that horses--- Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself? Just remember, say, ‘This is the way we used to do it.’” After the comments garnered significant attention, Murphy acknowledged regretting the remarks and explained that he had contacted Yankees general manager Brian Cashman to clarify that he was not specifically criticizing New York’s 2026 team. With Bauers now receiving the financial reward Murphy anticipated, instead from the Yankees’ biggest rival, the manager’s latest comments suggest he is at peace with losing the key player to a big market contract. item.title: Bud Dupree Tipped to Retire in a ‘Couple Months’ After Chargers Refuse to Grant Him Exit
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CA – NOVEMBER 09: Los Angeles Chargers outside linebacker Bud Dupree 48 during the NFL, American Football Herren, USA game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Los Angeles Chargers on November 09, 2025, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire NFL: NOV 09 Steelers at Chargers EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon20251108196 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Bud Dupree’s plea to leave the Chargers has caught a lot of attention, but the team has still not agreed to his request. However, it seems they might take some time to make a decision because of one specific reason pointed out by Breiden Fehoko. “They won’t release Bud because he’ll tell everything that went wrong this year,” former Chargers defensive lineman Breiden Fehoko said on his X page . “Funny part is he’ll do it anyway when he becomes a free agent and retires in a couple months.” Fehoko replied to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler’s X post, which read, “Chargers edge rusher Bud Dupree has requested his release this week, per sources. He also did so before the season. The Chargers have not granted it.” This situation comes after Dupree expressed his frustration with the team’s front office. He was unhappy with how the team’s management was handling things and told reporters to question the people making decisions for the Chargers instead of blaming the players. A veteran edge rusher's career hangs in the balance as contract disputes reshape his final chapter. Stay subscribed for the latest on how this standoff unfolds. “Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them,” Dupree said to the media. “Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull their cameras out and go upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them.” Another reason for his frustration could be his limited playing time. According to Pro Football Talk, Dupree has started only five games in his three seasons with the Chargers. His playing time has also dropped sharply this season. He played 23 defensive snaps in Week 1, 19 in Week 2, 16 in Week 3, and 13 in Week 4. By Week 5, he was given only two snaps before missing Week 6 because of an injury. After the team’s bye week, Dupree did not play any defensive snaps in Weeks 8 and 9. He was used only on special teams, playing seven snaps in Week 8 and 14 in Week 9. Dupree also dealt with a neck injury during the 2026 season. He suffered it in the third quarter of the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Denver Broncos on October 11. The injury forced him to miss the following game, but he returned after sitting out for one week. However, that was not the reason behind his absence from the Ravens game. He was medically available, but the Chargers chose not to include him in the lineup. Now, letting Bud Dupree go is a bit complicated. Since the NFL trade deadline passed on November 10, 2026, the Chargers can no longer trade him to another team during this season. However, they can still release him. item.title: Gary Woodland withdraws from Tiger Woods’ PGA Tour event and reveals the reason why
item.description: Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images Gary Woodland had somewhat of a renaissance season in 2026. In 2023, he underwent brain surgery to remove a benign tumor from his brain, which was pressing against a part of his brain that controls fear responses. Woodland has since suffered from PTSD, which he opened up about this year. It’s mightily impressive, therefore, that the 42-year-old returned to winning ways this year, claiming victory at the Houston Open. He finished in the top five twice this season, and is now ranked in the top 50 in the world. Woodland’s play in 2026 earned him a place at Tiger Woods’ Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, but unfortunately his health struggles have continued to end the year. He withdrew from the tournament and took to social media to explain the reason why. Gary Woodland explains withdrawal from Hero World Challenge Luckily, Woodland’s withdrawal has nothing to do with his 2023 brain surgery. Instead, it’s a knee injury that required surgery and has ruled him out of Woods’ event. The 2019 US Open winner took to social media to explain his withdrawal: “Just a brief health update for everyone (don’t worry, my brain is fine!). I’ve been feeling some discomfort in my knee, and after consulting with doctors, had an arthroscopic knee surgery last night at the Hospital for Special Surgery in NY with Dr. Riley Williams. “Everything went great and I should be back hitting balls in a few weeks and ready to start the 27 PGA Tour season better than ever. “Unfortunately, that does mean I have to withdraw from the Hero World Challenge, but I am so appreciative of Tiger and the team at TGR for offering me the invite and I look forward to making a return there in the future.” It’s unfortunate for Woodland, whose play this year earned him a place at this event alongside the world’s best players. Instead, it’ll be Keegan Bradley teeing off in Albany, taking Woodland’s spot after his withdrawal. item.title: Caleb Wilson shares when he’ll be back playing for the Chicago Bulls after fracturing his hand
item.description: Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images Caleb Wilson was the talk of the town in Chicago with his performances for the Bulls in the first few games of this season. The rookie played the first 10 games and averaged 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.9 assists, and many have since viewed him as the future of the franchise. Wilson is currently sidelined due to an injury, but he is anticipating a quick return to action. Caleb Wilson says he will be back in a couple of weeks During a game against the San Antonio Spurs, Wilson fractured his right hand while swiping at the ball in Victor Wembanyama’s grip. The 20-year-old scored 15 points and recorded five rebounds before going off, and the injury was expected to keep him on the sidelines for some time. On Friday, Wilson spoke to reporters, and he claimed that it is not a long-term injury and that he should be back as early as in a couple of weeks. He said, as per Joel Lorenzi on X : “I looked down on my hand, and it was bent the wrong way. I knew something was up and I heard it. “I mean, it’s difficult, but it’s not long-term. I’ll play again in a couple of weeks. I’m not really worried about it. It gives me an opportunity to get in shape, learn more about the game from a different view on the bench. So I’m excited.” When pressed about his ‘couple of weeks’ timeline, Wilson backtracked a bit, but he still seemed confident that he would be back soon. He said: “I don’t have an expectation on the timeline, but I just expect to be playing soon. I don’t expect this to be season-ending or make me miss a whole bunch of games. “I expect to play whenever I feel good, and I feel like I’ll feel good in a good amount of time.” The Chicago Bulls haven’t had a good season at all, but they have picked up a few wins since Wilson suffered his injury and has been unavailable. With the rookie playing, the Bulls won just one of their first nine games. Since his absence, they have won three of their five fixtures. That being said, Wilson is an incredible talent, and despite what the numbers say, we think the Bulls are a far better side when he’s fit and available for them. item.title: ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle. “The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.” Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most capped player’s rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. item.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
item.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

item.title: 2027: We’re not joining your opposition coalition, PDP tells Lukman
item.description: …Snubs November 30 summit, declares Wike’s Rainbow alliance its only coalition By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former National Vice Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Salihu Lukman, declaring that it will not attend the coalition’s November 30 summit. The party said it had not entered into any alliance with the coalition, authorised anyone to represent it at the summit or agreed to be bound by any decision taken in its name. It maintained that its only recognised coalition arrangement was the Rainbow Coalition, backed by its National Leader, Nyesom Wike. The position was contained in a statement signed by the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, who said those being presented as the party’s representatives were expelled members with no authority to speak or act on its behalf. Jungudo said the individuals’ claims to the party’s leadership and representation had suffered defeats at the Federal High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court. He added that the courts had issued orders restraining Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, and his associates from parading themselves as PDP leaders, while imposing financial penalties exceeding N100 million over alleged abuses of court processes and frivolous litigation. Questioning Lukman’s continued engagement with the individuals, Jungudo said, “It is therefore astonishing that Mr Salihu Lukman, who ought to be sufficiently informed about the legal status and recognised leadership of the PDP, would continue to engage these individuals and use them as a basis for associating the party with his so-called Toronto Coalition.” Describing the proposed arrangement as a political project built on misrepresentation, the PDP declared it ‘dead on arrival’, particularly because those being presented as its representatives lacked the authority to speak on its behalf. The party also threatened legal action against Lukman, his associates and other promoters of the Coalition for Democracy if they continued to use its name and institutional identity in their political activities. “The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” Jungudo warned. Reiterating its position, the party said the Rainbow Coalition, in line with Wike’s political direction and directives, remained its only recognised coalition arrangement. It consequently urged Nigerians, political stakeholders, members and supporters, as well as media organisations, to disregard reports linking its national headquarters at Wadata Plaza, Abuja, to the November 30 summit or any other political arrangement being promoted by Lukman and his associates. “The PDP will not allow its identity to be hijacked, its institutional authority misrepresented or its political interests compromised by individuals who

item.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
item.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. item.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
item.description: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. item.title: Young Protesters Hit Streets Across Europe
item.description: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people. Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks. The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities. But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations. Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets. “If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters. Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries. Protesters dressed up as clowns jump during a youth demonstration under the motto “Stop ReArm Europe!” ‘Lost So Much Hope’ In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide. “Austerity is social violence,” read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: “Be vegan, but eat the rich.” The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported. In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service. “I simply think it’s indefensible… to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP. While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing. Several hundred protesters, some in school uniform, gathered at demonstrations in London outside parliament and in nearby Trafalgar Square, waving placards that said “save higher education” and “Fight for our futures not their wars”. “I’ve lost so much hope,” Eliz, who had taken the day off from college and gave only one name, told AFP.
